original_value: In this paper, we propose Auracle, a wearable earpiece that can automatically recognize eating behavior. More specifically, in free-living conditions, we can recognize when and for how long a person is eating. Using an off-the-shelf contact microphone placed behind the ear, Auracle captures the sound of a person chewing as it passes through the bone and tissue of the head. This audio data is then processed by a custom analog/digital circuit board. To ensure reliable (yet comfortable) contact between microphone and skin, all hardware components are incorporated into a 3D-printed behind-the-head framework. We collected field data with 14 participants for 32 hours in free-living conditions and additional eating data with 10 participants for 2 hours in a laboratory setting. We achieved accuracy exceeding 92.8% and F1 score exceeding 77.5% for eating detection. Moreover, Auracle successfully detected 20-24 eating episodes (depending on the metrics) out of 26 in free-living conditions. We demonstrate that our custom device could sense, process, and classify audio data in real time. Additionally, we estimate Auracle can last 28.1 hours with a 110 mAh battery while communicating its observations of eating behavior to a smartphone over Bluetooth.

result.paraphrase: This paper introduces Auracle, a wearable earpiece designed to automatically detect eating behavior. In free-living settings, it can identify when a person is eating and the duration of each eating episode. Auracle uses an off-the-shelf contact microphone mounted behind the ear to capture chewing sounds as they travel through the bones and tissue of the head, and a custom analog/digital circuit board processes the resulting audio. For reliable yet comfortable skin contact, the hardware is integrated into a 3D-printed behind-the-head frame. We gathered field data from 14 participants over 32 hours in free-living conditions, plus additional eating data from 10 participants over 2 hours in a laboratory setting. For eating detection, it achieved accuracy above 92.8% and an F1 score above 77.5%. It also detected 20–24 eating episodes out of 26 in free-living conditions, depending on the metric. We show that the device can sense, process, and classify audio in real time, and estimate that Auracle can operate for 28.1 hours on a 110 mAh battery while sending its eating-behavior observations to a smartphone via Bluetooth.
